problem: For which of the following vector fields is $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}$ a potential function?

activity_context.topic_title: Conservative Vector Fields in the Cartesian Plane

feedback.problem: For which of the following vector fields is $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy-z)$ a potential function?
feedback.worked_solution:
A vector field $F$ is conservative if it is the gradient of a scalar function $f.$ That is, there exists a function $f$ such that $F=∇f.$ The function $f$ is called a potential function for $F.$

To compute the vector field associated with a potential function $f,$ we compute its gradient.

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\,i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\,j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy-z))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy-z))\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy-z))\,k \\  & =y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy-z)\,i+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy-z)\,j-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy-z)\,k \\  & =F\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field that has $f$ as a potential function is

$$
F=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy-z)\,i+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy-z)\,j-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy-z)\,k.
$$
